A consistent way to judge

Compare each output with the input and visible target. Choose the completion you would prefer to use overall.

  1. Look for a plausible whole object, including its shape and missing parts.
  2. Check whether color, texture, pattern, and identity remain consistent with visible evidence.
  3. Notice lost visible details, distorted geometry, or added objects.

Select more than one option when they are equally good. “Cannot judge” means the evidence is insufficient; it is different from a tie. Skip when you need to return later or an image is broken.

Shape and surface preferences are optional, separate judgements. They do not replace your overall choice. Use the same interpretation throughout the round.

The cropped views share one coordinate frame and scale. Open full resolution to inspect details. The visible SAM target is a detector reference, not the true hidden shape.

Ratings are saved in this browser. Export JSON after every session; use it to resume elsewhere. CSV is for inspection. No ratings are submitted automatically.
